newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Issues well-bid, junk sloppy.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Issues well-bid, junk sloppy.

text.p: Nearly $2.5 billion in supply found adequate demand in the U.S. high-grade corporate bond market and secondary spreads were only slightly shaken, dealers said.
Meanwhile, a host of high-yield issues also priced in a market that some traders referred to as "sloppy".

Large investment-grade deals, including Poland's $400 million in Yankee bonds, were said to be issue bid both before and after formal pricings. Poland's $300 million in seven-year debt will yield 75 basis points over Treasuries, while $100 million in 20-year debt was priced at 100 basis points over.
Poland was priced via J.P. Morgan Securities.
Other high-grade issues holding at issued levels include British Aerospace Finance Inc's $700 million two-part debt and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's $350 million two-tranche debt, traders said.

The British Aerospace issue was comprised of $200 million in 10-year notes priced at 58 basis points over Treasuries and $500 million 40-year debt at 78 basis points over. RJR's $200 million 10-year notes were priced at 215 basis points over, while another $150 million seven-year debt came at a spread of 195 basis points over the curve.
J.P. Morgan Securities led the British Aerospace issue and Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter, Discover & Co and Merrill Lynch & Co led the RJR deal.

Investors were also faced with $250 million seven-year notes from Hertz Corp at 55 basis points over via Merrill Lynch; $250 million five-year debentures at 50 basis points over via Goldman Sachs & Co; and $275 million seven- and 10-year notes from CarrAmerica Realty at 78 and 93 basis points over, respectively, via J.P. Morgan.

Dealers said persistent pressure on the 10-year part of the curve left spreads marginally wider there. But prices in general were under pressure as profit-taking and this week's burgeoning corporate supply conspired to deflate U.S. Treasuries, analysts said.
In high-yields, several new issues priced but were reportedly sagging with the broad market near the close.

Ocean Energy Inc's $200 million B3/B-minus rated 10-year senior subordinated notes, which priced at 99.83 to yield 245 basis points over the curve by Merrill Lynch, were quoted lower at 99.625 shortly after freed.
Some traders opined the buyside was more saturated with new issues than many had originally thought. Dealers themselves were also reportedly heavy with new paper.
"There's money coming into the funds but not enough to cover these new issues and money managers have to dump something in order to have new issue money," said one trader at a big shop in New York.

High-yield issues priced on Thursday also included $600 million 10-year Ba3/BB-minus rated senior unsecured notes from Indah Kiat Finance Mauritius Ltd priced to yield 10.105 percent through Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter, Discover & Co and $100 million 10-year B2/B-plus rated senior notes from Brazos Sportswear Inc priced to yield 10.625 via Dillon Read & Co.
In the Treasury market, the 30-year bond closed down 17/32 to yield 6.78 percent. The 10-year T-note closed off 10/32 to yield 6.49 percent.
